clue.text: Hands instrument to cheat

parts.note: hands are the sets of playing cards dealt to each player
the harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: Someone passes a musical instrument across so as to swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' looks like a verb meaning passes, but it is the noun: the hands dealt in a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler who wins at card games by trickery is the person meant by a cheat.

clue.text: Copper to hinder movement of plant

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to cumber is to burden or hamper, holding back free movement

explanation.surface: A policeman tries to stop a plant from moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer, but here it gives its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The trailing vine of the gourd family that bears long green salad fruits is a plant.

clue.text: Cecil took one article from the country

parts.note: Cecil Rhodes was the British imperialist businessman of southern Africa
the Roman numeral for one is I
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Cecil Rhodes removed something from the land he colonised.
explanation.walkthrough: The former African colony (now Zambia and Zimbabwe) was named after Cecil Rhodes, so the surface fits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a former British colony in southern Africa, so it names a country.

clue.text: Unexpected prompt

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean happening quickly: abrupt and without warning, or swift and immediate.

clue.text: Downright rascally

explanation.definitionFit: The word means utter or thoroughgoing, as in an out-and-out fool, and in an old sense meant roguish or knavish.

clue.text: Father, monk went round Georgia and Norway, heathen countries!

indicators.note: the father and the monk together surround the letters for the state and the country, so they go round them

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
Dom is the title given to a Benedictine monk
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A priest and a monk travel round Georgia and Norway, finding them pagan lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went round' makes the father-and-monk pair a container; 'and' only joins the two places. Dom is the courtesy title of Benedictine monks.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -dom makes a realm, so this is the realm of pagans: the non-Christian world.

clue.text: Derrick part returned to where in France one finds a jewel

indicators.note: returned means the derrick part is read backwards

parts.note: the jib is the projecting arm of a crane or derrick
où is French for where

explanation.surface: Part of a crane goes back to a spot in France where a gem is found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns JIB into BIJ; OU is the French word for 'where'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a small elegant thing, and as a noun is used for a trinket or gem.

clue.text: Report that the gun is loaded

explanation.definitionFit: A news announcement is a report; read as two words, a round in the chamber says a firearm is ready to fire.

clue.text: Ear job performed on rodent

indicators.note: an operation performed on the ear rearranges these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Ear surgery is carried out on a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The jumping desert animal with long hind legs is a small rodent.

clue.text: Concealed passage not prepared for translation

explanation.definitionFit: Hidden from sight is one sense; in exams, a text given without prior preparation for translating is the other.

clue.text: Cowherd stirred the soup

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A cattle herdsman stirs the soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred' looks like the cook's action but signals the anagram of COWHERD.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick creamy American seafood stew is a kind of soup.

clue.text: A bridal covering said to be from Elba ready to use

indicators.note: said shows that the bridal covering is spoken, and a word sounding like it is written

parts.note: a bride wears a veil

indicators.note: from Elba read in the backward direction, as in the palindrome about Napoleon on Elba

explanation.surface: A bride's veil is reported to have come from Elba.
explanation.walkthrough: VAIL sounds like VEIL ('said'); ELBA read backwards gives ABLE, 'from' signalling the reversal, as in the palindrome 'Able was I ere I saw Elba'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obtainable and on hand is ready to use.

clue.text: Stain be removed from a hard hat

indicators.note: the stain is shifted, so these letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A mark should be cleaned off a helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' suggests cleaning, but signals the anagram of STAINBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A light medieval steel helmet is a protective hard hat.

clue.text: Go off the rails?

parts.note: not a breakdown in behaviour but literally getting off a railway carriage

explanation.definitionFit: To leave a railway carriage at a station is to step off the rails, literally.

clue.text: What a secretary does when she tells the time?

definitions.text: What a secretary does when she tells the time?

parts.words: What a secretary does when she tells the time?
parts.note: a secretary reads out the record of a meeting; telling the time is reading the clock's small divisions

explanation.definitionFit: At a meeting the secretary announces the record of the last one, and reading a clock means noting its sixty-second units.

clue.text: Stop one on a horse

parts.note: to stall is to stop, as an engine does
the Roman numeral for one is I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone mounted on a horse brings it to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse is a breeding horse.

clue.text: For a worker to grasp? Shake on it!

explanation.definitionFit: A handle for gripping a tool is one sense; a clasp of hands, as when sealing a deal, is the other.

clue.text: River in Devon initially had wood from a tropical tree?

parts.note: the Tamar is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall
taken as written

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of Devon is taken

explanation.surface: A river in Devon is said to have had timber from a tropical tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is the river forming the border between Devon and Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The leguminous tree of Africa and Asia bearing sour pods is a tropical tree.

clue.text: Heavenly chips are cooked!

indicators.note: cooked describes the chips being worked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone praises fried potatoes as divine once they are done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are cooked' signals the anagram of CHIPSARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Like an angel of the highest order, so serene and heavenly.

clue.text: Unfortunately I cannot hold

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests something gone wrong, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Sadly someone admits they are unable to keep hold.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something is to keep it within, as a box keeps its contents.

clue.text: Large number leave prayer ring

indicators.note: leave means the large number is taken out of the prayer

parts.note: a collect is a short prayer read in church services
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number

explanation.surface: Many people walk out of a prayer meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: A collect is a short liturgical prayer; removing one C leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A collar or band that grips a tool or holds a gem in its setting is a ring.

clue.text: It might be sung with le el

annotationWithheld.clue: It might be sung with le el

clue.text: After Monday, more disintegration of the simplest of compounds

indicators.note: disintegration breaks up the following word, so its letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: After Monday, things fall further apart, down to basic chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just places the anagram behind the day; 'disintegration of' rearranges the four letters of 'more'.
explanation.definitionFit: A single molecular unit that links into chains to form a polymer is a basic chemical building block.

clue.text: Not such shiny stuff

explanation.definitionFit: Duller in finish, more matt, is one sense; physical substance is the other.

clue.text: Friend in clutches of fellow upsetting a highly inflammable liquid

indicators.note: being held in the clutches of something means being placed inside it
in a down clue upsetting turns the word for fellow upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a fellow is a man
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend held by an overturning man is splashed with something flammable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' suits a down clue, where reversing turns the word upside down; 'in clutches of' then holds the friend inside that reversed fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: This jellied petrol used in incendiary weapons is a highly inflammable substance.

clue.text: People in this get plenty of publicity

definitions.text: People in this get plenty of publicity

parts.words: People in this get plenty of publicity
parts.note: describes the glare of public attention, named after an old theatre spotlight

explanation.definitionFit: Being the centre of public attention, like a performer under a stage spotlight, brings plenty of exposure.

clue.text: Like amphibian at a bowl!

parts.note: in some dialects to is used for at, as in 'he's to home'
a bowl is a dish

explanation.surface: Someone at a bowl, croaking like a frog.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer split as three words gives a phrase meaning at a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Resembling a warty frog-like creature is being like an amphibian.

clue.text: Go about lunch-time to the city

indicators.note: about means the word for go is placed around the other piece

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game
lunch-time is one o'clock, and one is I

explanation.surface: Head off around midday to the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Lunch-time is taken as one o'clock, so it gives I, the Roman one, inside TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Piedmont in northern Italy is a city.

clue.text: Supplementing curative work of doctor who literally drops in

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means ancillary to medical work; as a noun it also means a medical orderly who parachutes in.
